description_full: Eregli Demir ve Çelik Fabrikalari T.A.S., together with its subsidiaries, produces and sells iron and steel rolled products, alloyed and non-alloyed iron, cast and pressed steel, coke, and by-products in Turkey and internationally. The company offers flat steel products, including hot and cold rolled flat steel, plate, tin, chrome, and galvanized coated sheets. It also engages in the production of integrated and electrical steel; renewable energy generation; industrial gas production and sale; pellets; iron and magnesite ores; refractory; trading; recycling; and special purpose business. In addition, the company offers after-sales, laboratory and calibration, steel service center, and port services; and management and consulting services. Further, it exports its products. The company serves the automotive, white goods, tube mills, rolling mills, general manufacturing, electric&electronics, machinery, energy, heating equipment, shipbuilding, defense, packaging, and renewable energy industries. Eregli Demir ve Çelik Fabrikalari T.A.S. was founded in 1960 and is headquartered in Istanbul, Turkey.

financial_summary: Eregli Demir Ve Celik Fabrikal is a mid-cap basic materials business with a $4.3B market cap on $4.1B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at -12% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome. Operating margins are contracting by -4.6pp, the first warning that competitive pressure is eroding the franchise.

Returns on capital run at 4% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 10% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $987M in free cash flow — roughly 24 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 127.11× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.1× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and thin 0.8× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield is only 0.8%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and profit capture is only 0.3× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
